title: Standard changelog, index and citation hygiene
cluster_summary: Every finding is real and every fix lands in WowAddonStandards. The only ordering dependency is that dev-copilot H-01 must land before the changelog move. The one finding with recurring cost is WAS-R-03: 92% of the index (384 KB) is changelog, and every audit, review and harvest run reads it. Moving it to its own file is worth doing, but the review bundle still marks C-02 'owner decision required', so it goes to the owner as a should, gated on approval and on H-01. The live-text citation errors (library-stack.md:223 and AUDIT.md:994 citing documentation-§5 for the scheme in §6, and documentation.md:259 citing item 8 for item 6) should be fixed in one citation commit. WAS-A-13 and WAS-R-12 overlap, so merge them. The changelog typos, the reorder and the README wording go into the C-02 move when it lands, or into a small standalone edit if it does not. Replace the footer date with no date at all. The TL;DR rename is not worth doing on its own.

verdicts.assessment: All three are verified on the branch. documentation.md:259 is live normative text: it sends readers to documentation-§1 item 8 (Troubleshooting) when it means item 6 (How <it> works), so it is worth fixing. The two STANDARDS.md fragments (:120 preview-mode-§, :168 automated-tests-§?) are historical changelog typos and essentially free to fix. The :120 part duplicates WAS-R-12.
verdicts.remediation: documentation.md:259: change 'documentation-§1 item 8' to 'item 6'. STANDARDS.md:120: change 'preview-mode-§' to 'preview-mode' (absorbs WAS-R-12). STANDARDS.md:168: change 'automated-tests-§?' to 'automated-tests-§3'. Use one commit, together with WAS-R-06. If C-02 lands first, the two changelog edits apply in the moved changelog file.

verdicts.assessment: v2.19.0 at :218 sits between v2.17.1 and v2.17.0. standards/README.md:13 says 'changelog at its top', which contradicts :32 and CLAUDE.md:83-84, and :32 itself skips over 'Related documents'. This is cosmetic and a convention, not a MUST, and C-02 rewrites the same wording anyway.
verdicts.remediation: Fold this into C-02: reorder v2.19.0 above v2.18.0 during the move, and rewrite the location wording in standards/README.md:13/:32 (and the dev-copilot wow-harvest-standards.md:152 'at the top' phrase through H-01). If C-02 is declined, make the standalone fix: move the v2.19.0 entry above v2.18.0 and make README:13 match :32, naming the ## Changelog section after Related documents.

verdicts.assessment: The measurements hold: 418,659 bytes, of which 384,409 (92%) is changelog. That cost recurs on every agent run that reads the index, and it grows with every release. Still, keeping the changelog in the index is a documented design choice (CLAUDE.md:82-84), and docs/reviews/2026-10-07/02_PROPOSED_CHANGES.md:101 still marks C-02 'owner decision required'. The finding's 'owner decision, v2.77.0' therefore overstates its status. The file name (changelog.md vs CHANGELOG.md) is also an open owner call (02_PROPOSED_CHANGES.md:37).
verdicts.remediation: Ask the owner to approve C-02. If approved: land dev-copilot H-01 first (wow-harvest-standards.md:152, agents/wow-standards-audit.md:108 point at the new file and stop describing the index as carrying the changelog). Then move STANDARDS.md ## Changelog verbatim to standards/CHANGELOG.md (or changelog.md, owner's choice), leave the current entry plus a 'Full history' pointer, list the file under Related documents (not Sections), and update CLAUDE.md:82-84/:135, standards/README.md:13/:32, README.md section A step 4, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the DEPENDENCIES.md file count. Bump to v2.77.0. Absorb WAS-A-18 and the changelog parts of WAS-A-13 and WAS-R-12.

verdicts.assessment: documentation.md:525 is '### 5. Keeping docs in sync' and :529 is '### 6. Standards reference'. library-stack.md:223 (the live LibKa0s applicability table) and AUDIT.md:994 ('documentation-§5/§6') send auditors to the wrong subsection. These are one-line fixes to live normative text.
verdicts.remediation: library-stack.md:223: change the row to 'documentation-§6 | The filename-§N citation scheme and its citation rules.' AUDIT.md:994: change 'documentation-§5/§6' to 'documentation-§6'. Use the same commit as WAS-A-13.

verdicts.assessment: The STANDARDS.md:255 footer says 'Authoritative as of 2026-10-01', but the header is v2.76.1, 2026-10-07. The footer is a redundant copy of the stamp that keeps drifting. It misleads nobody about any rule, because the header is authoritative. scripts/check-standard.sh does not exist yet (C-03).
verdicts.remediation: Remove the date from the footer so the header stays the single authority: '**End of index. The normative rules live in the section files linked above.**' Add a stamp-consistency check only if C-03's check-standard.sh is adopted separately.

verdicts.assessment: The summary really is 4,733 words under a 'One-page TL;DR' label, but the label appears in six places (EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:3, standards/README.md:12, STANDARDS.md:89, CLAUDE.md:50, README.md:61/:143). Renaming it changes no reader's behaviour and no audit's accuracy, and the real problem, a duplicated second copy, is explicitly deferred.
STANDARDS.md:120 has 'preview-mode-§' with no number, and preview-mode.md has no numbered subsections. This duplicates the :120 part of WAS-A-13: a cosmetic typo in a historical changelog entry.
verdicts.remediation: Merge into WAS-A-13: change 'preview-mode-§' to 'preview-mode' (in the moved changelog file if C-02 lands first).
